I got firm numbers for eight of the ten providers. For AWS RDS and Tiger, the 4 GB price wasn't on the pages I could read, so those two rows are incomplete. I didn't use any provider's online calculator.

| Provider | Cheapest ~4 GB plan | Monthly price | Included storage | Backup retention | PITR | Free tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Neon** | Launch, 1 CU (about 4 GB), always-on | about $77 compute (0.106 × 730 h), plus $0.35/GB-mo storage | None; usage-billed | Up to 7 days of history, configurable | Extra: history window billed at $0.20/GB-mo of changed data | Yes, no time limit: 1 GB per project, up to 8 GB RAM |
| **Supabase** | Pro ($25) plus Medium compute ($60, 4 GB shared), minus $10 compute credit | **$75** | 8 GB disk on Pro (from memory; not on the pages I read) | 7 days of daily backups | Extra: $100/mo per 7 days of retention | Yes, but projects pause after 1 week of inactivity, and PITR isn't available |
| **Render** | Basic-style 1 CPU / 4 GB | **$55** (2 CPU / 4 GB is $75) | 1 GB, then $0.30/GB | Logical backups, plus a PITR window of 3 days (Hobby workspace) or 7 days (Pro workspace) | Included | Yes, 256 MB, with limitations |
| **Railway** | No managed Postgres; self-run on a volume | about $40 RAM ($10/GB) plus CPU ($20/vCPU) plus volume ($0.15/GB), on a $5 Hobby or $20 Pro plan | Pay per GB | Volume backups only | No true PITR | $5 trial credit; Free plan gives $1/mo |
| **Fly.io** | No 4 GB tier. Starter is 2 GB at $72; Launch is 8 GB at $282 | $72 or $282 | Billed at $0.28/GB | 10 days (from a Fly community post) | Restore to a point in time via `fly mpg restore` | No |
| **DigitalOcean** | 4 GiB / 2 vCPU | **$60.90** | The slug says 80 GiB; the pricing table shows a 60–120 GiB range at $0.215/GiB | 7 days of daily backups | Included | No; new accounts get small credits |
| **Aiven** | Startup, 4 GB (the page says "from $75", 4–192 GB) | **$75** | 80 GB minimum | 2 days | Included (2-day window) | Yes, no time limit: 1 GB RAM, 1 GB storage |
| **Crunchy Bridge** | Standard-4 or Hobby-4, 4 GB | **$70** | None; $0.10/GB extra | 10 days, longer if you configure it | Included | No |
| **Tiger (Timescale)** | Not found. Performance compute "starts at $30" | Unverified | Storage $0.177/GB-mo | 3 days of PITR on Performance, 14 days on Scale | Included | 30-day trial with a $1,000 credit |
| **AWS RDS** | db.t4g.medium (4 GB) | Not on the page I read | gp3 storage billed separately | 7 days by default in the console, up to 35 | Included, but backup storage beyond your provisioned size is billed | Not checked |

**Where the numbers are incomplete**
- **Tiger:** the page only gives "compute starts at $30". I couldn't find a 4 GB price, so use their pricing calculator or trial for that.
- **AWS RDS:** the pricing table didn't render. I believe db.t4g.medium Postgres is roughly $47/mo single-AZ in us-east-1, but that's from memory and unchecked. AWS's calculator is the right way to confirm it.
- **Aiven:** the page says the Startup plan runs 4–192 GB and starts at $75. I took $75 to be the 4 GB plan, but it doesn't say so outright.
- **Railway:** the monthly figure is my own estimate from per-GB and per-vCPU rates. I didn't check backup retention for Railway or Fly's separate Postgres docs.
- **Regions:** I didn't confirm a US region for each provider.
- **Free tiers:** Supabase, Aiven and Neon are the real ongoing ones. Render's free Postgres has strict limits.

**Cheapest 4 GB with PITR included**
- Render at $55, though its PITR window is only 3 days unless you're on a Pro workspace.
- Crunchy Bridge ($70) and DigitalOcean ($60.90) have PITR included with longer windows, but storage is billed on top for Crunchy.
- Supabase works out to about $175/mo once you add PITR.

The scraped pages are saved in `/tmp/fceval-a1-t1-gsm469pv/work/.firecrawl/`.

How reliable each number is:
- **Michigan State:** The MSU controller page lists tuition of $8,828 per semester for freshmen, so $17,656 a year. I added the recreation and wellness fee ($170 per semester) and the student voted taxes ($37.50 per semester) to get about $18,071. MSU's admissions page still shows an older tuition figure ($16,916). US News lists $19,742 for 2026-27, which I could not reconcile with MSU's own pages.
- **Indiana, Nebraska, Oregon, Rutgers:** These are the schools' own cost-of-attendance or tuition pages, not a bursar rate sheet. I didn't confirm that the Indiana and Nebraska pages are the final 2026-27 figures. Rutgers' own page calls its 2026-27 rates estimates.
- **Illinois, Michigan, Rutgers:** Rates vary by college or major. I used the base or lower-division rate; engineering, business and some other majors cost more.
- **Wisconsin:** The financial aid office shows $12,532, which includes other items. I used the bursar's tuition-plus-segregated-fee total.
- **Iowa and Maryland:** Business, engineering and computer science students pay more.
- **Washington, Rutgers and Oregon:** One-time or program-specific fees are not counted. Oregon, for example, adds a one-time $569.89 matriculation fee.

I couldn't get firm prices for two of the ten. The AWS page doesn't list instance prices, and Tiger doesn't show a 4 GB price outside its calculator, which I didn't run. All figures are list prices pulled on 2026-10-20 from the vendors' own pages. The saved pages are in `/tmp/fceval-a1-t2-ml0vsdzv/work/.firecrawl/`.

| Provider | Cheapest ~4 GB plan | Monthly | Storage included | Backup retention | PITR | Free tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Neon** | Launch, 1 CU (≈4 GB), always on | ≈$77 compute (0.106 × 730 h), no monthly minimum | None; $0.35/GB-mo | Snapshots at $0.09/GB-mo | Included, up to a 7-day window. History storage is billed extra at $0.20/GB-mo. | Yes, up to 2 CU (8 GB), 1 GB storage, 6 h window. No time limit. |
| **Supabase** | Pro ($25) + Medium 4 GB (shared CPU) | $75 ($25 + $60 − $10 credit) | 8 GB disk, then $0.125/GB | 7 days of daily backups | **Extra:** $100/mo per 7 days of retention. It needs at least a Small compute add-on and replaces daily backups. | Yes, but projects pause after a week idle and are limited to 2 active. |
| **Render** | Postgres 1c-4g | $55 | 1 GB, then $0.30/GB | Logical backups kept 7 days | Included on paid instances: 3 days on Hobby workspace, 7 on Pro. | Yes, 256 MB RAM, with limits. |
| **Railway** | No managed Postgres product; it's a template on a volume | ≈$40 if 4 GB is held all month, plus CPU and the Pro seat (see note) | 0.5 GB on Free, up to 5 GB on Hobby, more on Pro | Daily backups kept 6 days | Available, writing WAL to a storage bucket you pay for. | Only a 30-day trial ($5 credit), then $1/mo. |
| **Fly.io** | No 4 GB plan. Starter is 2 GB ($72); Launch is 8 GB. | $282 | None; $0.28/GB | Not on the pricing page | Included. A Fly support reply in the community forum says 10 days. | No |
| **DigitalOcean** | Basic 4 GiB / 2 vCPU | $60.90 | 60 GiB (scales up to 120 GiB) | 7 days, daily | Included. The restore flow offers "choose a point in time". | No (only a $5 signup credit mentioned) |
| **Aiven** | Startup-4 (4 GB RAM, 80 GB) | $75 | 80 GB | PITR window is 2 days | Included on Startup and above (2 / 14 / 30 days on Startup / Business / Premium). | Yes: 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 GB storage, no region choice. |
| **Crunchy Bridge** | Hobby-4 or Standard-4 on AWS (1 vCPU, 4 GB) | $70 | None; $0.10/GB | 10 days, daily base backup plus WAL | Included in that 10-day window. | No |
| **Timescale (Tiger)** | Performance plan; 4 GB tier not shown | Not found. Compute starts at $30/mo, so a 4 GB tier is somewhere above that. | None; $0.177/GB-mo | Not stated | Included, to 3 days on Performance (14 on Scale). | 30-day trial only, no card. |
| **AWS RDS** | db.t4g.medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB), single-AZ | ≈$47 plus storage (my recollection of ≈$0.065/h, not verified) | None; gp3 is $0.115/GB-mo (via third-party search result) | Default 7 days, configurable up to 35 | Included. Backup storage is free up to the size of your database. | 12 months, 750 h/mo on micro instances, 20 GB |

**Calculators and gaps**
- **No calculator needed:** the prices for Neon, Supabase, Render, Fly, DigitalOcean, Aiven and Crunchy came straight from their pricing pages or docs.
- **AWS RDS:** the pricing page tells you to use the AWS Pricing Calculator for instance rates. The ≈$47 is my own estimate, so run the calculator before relying on it.
- **Tiger:** the 4 GB price is behind the sizing/calculator flow, which I didn't run.
- **Railway:** I estimated ≈$40 from the per-GB-second memory rate. Railway bills actual usage, so real cost depends on CPU and how much memory Postgres really uses. I didn't confirm the Pro seat fee.
- **Fly retention:** the 10-day figure comes from a forum reply from Fly support, not their docs. Fly's backup docs page returned a 404.
- **Render Pro:** the Pro workspace fee for the 7-day PITR window isn't included in the $55.
- **Aiven and Crunchy:** both are single-node or non-HA at these prices, and neither price includes an HA standby.

**Cheapest overall**
- **Cheapest overall:** AWS RDS is probably cheapest, but that figure is unverified.
- **Cheapest verified:** DigitalOcean at $60.90, which also includes 60 GiB of storage.
- **Best on PITR:** Crunchy Bridge at $70 includes 10 days of PITR in the price.
- **Costliest for PITR:** Supabase's $75 plan has no PITR, so adding it takes the total to about $175/mo.
